shadow-of-a-dot.title: The shadow of a dot
shadow-of-a-dot.summary: Drag a dot around a circle and discover what sine really is.

read-the-calliper.title: Read the calliper
read-the-calliper.summary: Main scale, then the division that lines up. The whole skill in two numbers.

the-bent-calliper.title: The bent calliper
the-bent-calliper.summary: This instrument lies by the same amount every time. Catch it, and correct it.

distance-and-displacement.title: There and back
distance-and-displacement.summary: Send a body out and watch it return. How far did it travel, and where did it end up?

reading-motion-graphs.title: Slope and area
reading-motion-graphs.summary: A velocity graph hides two answers: its slope and the space under it.

two-motions-at-once.title: Two motions at once
two-motions-at-once.summary: Steady across, accelerating down. Watch the ghosts and you can see both.

fired-from-a-cliff.title: Fired from a cliff
fired-from-a-cliff.summary: Fire it flat and fast, or just drop it. Which one lands first?

when-friction-gives-way.title: When friction gives way
when-friction-gives-way.summary: Push a block gently and nothing happens. Push harder and everything changes at once.

the-tilted-table.title: The tilted table
the-tilted-table.summary: Tilt the surface and the weight splits in two. One part presses, the other pulls.

the-energy-ledger.title: The energy ledger
the-energy-ledger.summary: Send a block up a slope. Nothing is lost — it just moves between two columns.

friction-takes-its-cut.title: Friction takes its cut
friction-takes-its-cut.summary: Gravity lends energy and gets it back. Friction charges a fee.

what-survives-a-crash.title: What survives a crash
what-survives-a-crash.summary: Two carts, one collision, and two bars that behave very differently.

bounce-and-rebound.title: Bounce and rebound
bounce-and-rebound.summary: Hit something heavy and you come straight back. Hit something equal and you stop dead.

the-turning-effect.title: The turning effect
the-turning-effect.summary: The same push, in two different places, does two very different things.

where-the-mass-sits.title: Where the mass sits
where-the-mass-sits.summary: Same mass, same radius, five arrangements — and five different answers.

newtons-cannonball.title: Newton's cannonball
newtons-cannonball.summary: Fire it sideways. Too slow and it lands; fast enough and it never does.

the-long-way-round.title: The long way round
the-long-way-round.summary: Stretch the orbit, and see what the period does — and does not — depend on.

the-wire-that-stretches.title: The wire that stretches
the-wire-that-stretches.summary: Hang weight on a steel wire and measure a stretch you could not see without help.

where-it-gives-way.title: Where it gives way
where-it-gives-way.summary: Past the elastic limit a wire stops springing back. Some materials warn you first; glass does not.

how-deep-is-deep.title: How deep is deep
how-deep-is-deep.summary: Take a pressure probe down a tank of water and find out what the reading actually depends on.

what-floats.title: What floats
what-floats.summary: Heavy things float and light things sink. Only one comparison actually matters.

the-stubborn-thermometer.title: The stubborn thermometer
the-stubborn-thermometer.summary: Heat 100 g of ice and watch the temperature climb — until it simply stops.

where-the-heat-hides.title: Where the heat hides
where-the-heat-hides.summary: Three quarters of the journey from ice to steam is spent standing still at 100 °C.

the-red-line.title: The red line of hydrogen
the-red-line.summary: Let an electron fall two rungs and catch the one colour of light it gives out.

series-and-limits.title: Series and limits
series-and-limits.summary: Where the electron lands decides the whole family of lines — and He⁺ can mimic hydrogen exactly.

half-and-half-again.title: Half, and half again
half-and-half-again.summary: Watch a reaction use up half its reactant, then half of what is left — always in the same time.

ten-degrees-hotter.title: Ten degrees hotter
ten-degrees-hotter.summary: A small rise in temperature, a big rise in speed — and why a high energy barrier makes it bigger still.

push-and-it-pushes-back.title: Push, and it pushes back
push-and-it-pushes-back.summary: Squeeze a cylinder of brown gas and watch the reaction shift to undo what you did.

the-haber-compromise.title: The Haber compromise
the-haber-compromise.summary: Make ammonia from the air: squeeze for yield, and find out why heating it is a trade-off.

one-drop.title: One drop
one-drop.summary: Run alkali into acid and find the single drop where the pH leaps from 4 to 10.

weak-acids-and-buffers.title: Weak acids and buffers
weak-acids-and-buffers.summary: Vinegar's acid fights back: a buffer, a pH equal to its pKa half-way, and an indicator to choose.

the-daniell-cell.title: The Daniell cell
the-daniell-cell.summary: Zinc, copper and a wire: read the voltage, find the anode, and work out E°cell from the series.

why-batteries-go-flat.title: Why batteries go flat
why-batteries-go-flat.summary: Concentration moves the voltage by the Nernst equation — and a flat battery is simply a reaction at equilibrium.

salt-on-the-road.title: Salt on the road
salt-on-the-road.summary: Why salted roads stay clear of ice: dissolved particles push the freezing point down.

pasta-water-and-pairs.title: Pasta water and pairs
pasta-water-and-pairs.summary: Solutions boil later, molecules that pair up count half, and osmosis pushes with atmospheres.

counting-by-weighing.title: Counting by weighing
counting-by-weighing.summary: Molecules are too small to count, so chemists weigh them: grams into moles, and a mass that never changes.

the-limiting-reagent.title: The limiting reagent
the-limiting-reagent.summary: Whichever reactant runs out first decides everything — and it is not always the one with less mass.

why-ice-melts.title: Why ice melts
why-ice-melts.summary: Melting takes in heat, yet ice melts by itself above 0 °C. The reason is one straight line.

four-kinds-of-reaction.title: Four kinds of reaction
four-kinds-of-reaction.summary: Always, never, only when hot, only when cold: the signs of ΔH and ΔS sort every reaction.

pairs-push-apart.title: Pairs push apart
pairs-push-apart.summary: Electron pairs spread as far apart as they can — and lone pairs push hardest of all.

beyond-eight.title: Beyond eight
beyond-eight.summary: Five and six electron pairs: see-saws, T-shapes, and a square with a lone pair above and below.

across-and-down.title: Across and down
across-and-down.summary: Atoms shrink across a row and grow down a column — the two ideas behind almost every trend.

the-exceptions.title: The exceptions
the-exceptions.summary: Ionisation enthalpy rises across a period — except where it does not, and those dips are the exam questions.

groups-and-valency.title: Groups and valency
groups-and-valency.summary: An element's place in the table gives its outer electrons — and with them its valency and how it reacts.

close-the-loop.title: Close the loop
close-the-loop.summary: A bulb, a cell and a switch. Make it light — then make it brighter.

conductor-or-insulator.title: Conductor or insulator?
conductor-or-insulator.summary: Put things in the gap and see which ones let electricity through.

where-fractions-live.title: Where fractions live
where-fractions-live.summary: Every fraction is a point on the number line. Find three quarters, and put fractions in order.

same-point-different-names.title: Same point, different names
same-point-different-names.summary: 3/4 and 6/8 land in exactly the same place. Find out why, and spot fractions that are secretly equal.

whole-numbers-and-decimals.title: Whole numbers and decimals
whole-numbers-and-decimals.summary: Whole numbers sit one step apart on the line. Cut each step into tenths and hundredths, and the decimals appear in between.

sour-bitter-or-neither.title: Sour, bitter or neither
sour-bitter-or-neither.summary: Lemons are sour, soap is bitter, water is neither. Sort the kitchen, and meet the colours that tell you which is which.

neutralise-it.title: Neutralise it
neutralise-it.summary: Add a base to an acid, drop by drop, until it cancels out — and watch the indicator say when.

how-fast.title: How fast?
how-fast.summary: A runner, a stopwatch and a measuring tape: speed is how far you go in each second.

the-journey-graph.title: The journey graph
the-journey-graph.summary: A distance–time graph is a journey drawn as a line. Flat means stopped; steep means fast.

heavy-is-not-the-question.title: Heavy is not the question
heavy-is-not-the-question.summary: A ship floats and a pin sinks. It is not about how heavy something is — it is about how much stuff is packed into it.

the-push-of-water.title: The push of water
the-push-of-water.summary: Dive deeper and the water presses harder. That same push holds up everything that floats.

melt-boil-change-back.title: Melt, boil, change back
melt-boil-change-back.summary: Heat ice until it melts, then boils. Watch the thermometer do something surprising in between.

can-you-undo-it.title: Can you undo it?
can-you-undo-it.summary: Melted ice freezes again, but burnt paper never comes back. Two kinds of change, and how to tell them apart.

shadow-play.title: Shadow play
shadow-play.summary: A lamp, a card and a screen. Make shadows grow and shrink, and find out what makes them dark.

mirror-mirror.title: Mirror, mirror
mirror-mirror.summary: Why a pinhole camera turns the world upside down, and the rule every mirror follows.

find-the-mystery-weight.title: Find the mystery weight
find-the-mystery-weight.summary: A box of unknown weight on a scale. Level it, and you have solved an equation.

same-to-both-sides.title: Same to both sides
same-to-both-sides.summary: No more guessing: take the same off both pans and the scale stays level — until the box is alone.

what-sticks.title: What sticks?
what-sticks.summary: A magnet picks up a nail but not a coin. Find out which things are magnetic.

poles-apart.title: Poles apart
poles-apart.summary: Two magnets can pull together or push apart. Find the rule, then follow a compass round a magnet.

counting-squares.title: Counting squares
counting-squares.summary: Area is how many squares a shape covers; perimeter is the walk round its edge. They are not the same thing.

filling-boxes.title: Filling boxes
filling-boxes.summary: How many cubes fit in a box? Build it layer by layer and the volume formula writes itself.

nets-and-surface-area.title: Nets and surface area
nets-and-surface-area.summary: Unfold a box and it lies flat as six rectangles. Count their squares and you have its surface area.

steady-or-speeding-up.title: Steady or speeding up?
steady-or-speeding-up.summary: Some things move at a steady speed; others speed up or slow down. Acceleration tells them apart.

area-under-the-graph.title: The area under the graph
area-under-the-graph.summary: A velocity–time graph hides the distance travelled in its area. Find it, and use it.

balanced-and-unbalanced.title: Balanced and unbalanced
balanced-and-unbalanced.summary: A push does not always make something move. What matters is the force left over.

bumps-and-bounces.title: Bumps and bounces
bumps-and-bounces.summary: A heavy, fast cart is hard to stop. Momentum measures it — and a collision never loses any.

lift-and-drop.title: Lift and drop
lift-and-drop.summary: Moving things have kinetic energy; raised things have potential energy. Watch one turn into the other.

energy-changes-form.title: Energy changes form
energy-changes-form.summary: Energy moves from kinetic to potential to heat — and not a joule of it disappears.

into-the-water.title: Into the water
into-the-water.summary: A mirror bounces light at equal angles; water and glass bend it. Find out how much.

through-a-lens.title: Through a lens
through-a-lens.summary: A convex lens can throw a picture on a screen or act as a magnifying glass. Where the object sits decides which.

ohms-law.title: Ohm's law
ohms-law.summary: More push, more current; more resistance, less. One rule ties them together.

series-or-parallel.title: Series or parallel?
series-or-parallel.summary: Join bulbs one after another and they dim; side by side, each shines fully. That is why houses are wired in parallel.

electron-shells.title: Electron shells
electron-shells.summary: Electrons fill shells 2, 8, 8 — and the outer shell decides how an atom reacts.

the-modern-table.title: The modern table
the-modern-table.summary: Rows are shells, columns are outer electrons. Read the periodic table straight from the atom.

isotopes-and-isobars.title: Isotopes and isobars
isotopes-and-isobars.summary: Same protons, different neutrons: isotopes. Same mass number, different elements: isobars.

making-waves.title: Making waves
making-waves.summary: A speaker shakes the air. Change the note and the loudness, and find where sound cannot go.

echoes.title: Echoes
echoes.summary: Clap at a wall and time the echo. There and back: t = 2d / v.

atoms-in-atoms-out.title: Atoms in, atoms out
atoms-in-atoms-out.summary: A reaction never makes or loses an atom. Count them, balance them, and weigh both sides.

balance-it.title: Balance it
balance-it.summary: Ammonia, cooking gas and rust — then sort reactions into combination, decomposition and displacement.

squares-on-the-sides.title: Squares on the sides
squares-on-the-sides.summary: Draw a square on every side of a right triangle, and the two small ones fill the big one.

sine-cosine-tangent.title: Sine, cosine, tangent
sine-cosine-tangent.summary: Name the sides from the angle, and their ratios measure a tower from the ground.

points-and-lines.title: Points and lines
points-and-lines.summary: Plot points in all four quadrants, then find the ones that sit on y = 2x + 1.

where-lines-meet.title: Where lines meet
where-lines-meet.summary: Two equations, two lines: the answer is where they cross — if they cross at all.

filling-the-boxes.title: Filling the boxes
filling-the-boxes.summary: Build atoms electron by electron: lowest energy first, two to a box, spread out before pairing.

shapes-and-nodes.title: Shapes and nodes
shapes-and-nodes.summary: n sets the size, l the shape and m the direction. Count the places an electron is never found.

faradays-laws.title: Faraday's laws
faradays-laws.summary: A current for a time is a charge; a charge is electrons; electrons make metal. Weigh what you plate.

ions-on-the-move.title: Ions on the move
ions-on-the-move.summary: Dilute a solution and each mole conducts better — a little for strong electrolytes, a lot for weak ones.

oxidation-numbers.title: Oxidation numbers
oxidation-numbers.summary: Numbers that track electrons: the one that rises is oxidised, the one that falls is reduced.

balance-the-electrons.title: Balance the electrons
balance-the-electrons.summary: Make the electrons lost equal the electrons gained — then decide whether the reaction goes at all.

cells-and-energy.title: Cells and energy
cells-and-energy.summary: Dry, mercury, lead–acid and fuel cells: their voltages, their energy, and what happens as they run down.

stopping-rust.title: Stopping rust
stopping-rust.summary: Rust needs water and oxygen. Paint, tin and zinc keep it off — but only zinc survives a scratch.

colour-and-magnetism.title: Colour and magnetism
colour-and-magnetism.summary: Count the d electrons of an ion: the unpaired ones make it magnetic, and any d–d jump makes it coloured.

variable-valency.title: Variable valency
variable-valency.summary: From scandium's single +3 to manganese's +7: why the middle of the row has the most oxidation states.

splitting-the-d-orbitals.title: Splitting the d orbitals
splitting-the-d-orbitals.summary: Six ligands push two d orbitals up and three down. The size of the gap decides the colour.

high-spin-low-spin.title: High spin, low spin
high-spin-low-spin.summary: Pair up or climb the gap? Compare Δo with the pairing energy — and read the answer off a magnet.

down-the-group.title: Down the group
down-the-group.summary: From carbon to lead, nitrogen to bismuth: non-metals become metals, and the heaviest keep an inert pair.

the-hydrides.title: The hydrides
the-hydrides.summary: NH₃, H₂O and HF break their groups' trends — hydrogen bonding. Bond angles close and bonds weaken down each group.

naming-complexes.title: Naming complexes
naming-complexes.summary: Ligands in alphabetical order, the metal, its oxidation state: read a complex's name straight from its formula.

cis-trans-and-mirrors.title: Cis, trans and mirrors
cis-trans-and-mirrors.summary: Same ligands, different places: cis and trans, fac and mer — and complexes that are left- and right-handed.

filling-the-mos.title: Filling the MOs
filling-the-mos.summary: Two atoms' orbitals make bonding and antibonding orbitals. Count the electrons in each to get the bond order.

why-oxygen-is-magnetic.title: Why oxygen is magnetic
why-oxygen-is-magnetic.summary: Two unpaired electrons in π* make O₂ stick to a magnet — and adding or removing electrons changes its bond.

counting-electrons.title: Counting electrons
counting-electrons.summary: Every valence electron goes in a bond or a lone pair. Share enough, and every atom gets an octet.

formal-charge-and-resonance.title: Formal charge and resonance
formal-charge-and-resonance.summary: When several structures give octets, the smallest formal charges win — and equal winners blend into one.

hot-and-cold.title: Hot and cold
hot-and-cold.summary: Negative ΔH gives heat out, positive takes it in — and twice the reaction, twice the heat.

hess-cycles.title: Hess cycles
hess-cycles.summary: Down to the elements and back up: work out any ΔH from formation enthalpies, or estimate it from bonds.

vapour-over-mixtures.title: Vapour over mixtures
vapour-over-mixtures.summary: Each liquid escapes in proportion to how much of it there is — and the vapour is richer in the eager one.

ideal-or-not.title: Ideal or not
ideal-or-not.summary: When A and B like each other more — or less — than themselves, the vapour pressure sags or bulges. And gases dissolve by pressure.

finding-the-order.title: Finding the order
finding-the-order.summary: Double the concentration and watch the rate: unchanged, doubled or quadrupled tells you the order.

straight-line-plots.title: Straight-line plots
straight-line-plots.summary: Each order has one plot that comes out straight, and its own kind of half-life.

collisions-that-count.title: Collisions that count
collisions-that-count.summary: Molecules collide all the time. Only the ones with enough energy, meeting the right way round, react.

whats-in-a-formula.title: What's in a formula
whats-in-a-formula.summary: Why chlorine weighs 35.45, how a molecule's mass is shared out, and the simplest ratio hiding in a formula.

how-strong-is-it.title: How strong is it?
how-strong-is-it.summary: The same flask described four ways: per litre of solution, per kilogram of water, as a share of the moles, as a share of the mass.

will-it-precipitate.title: Will it precipitate?
will-it-precipitate.summary: Every sparingly soluble salt has a limit, Ksp. Stay under it and the solution is clear; pass it and solid appears.

the-common-ion.title: The common ion
the-common-ion.summary: Add an ion the salt already has, and less of the salt dissolves — while Ksp stays exactly where it was.

finding-the-nucleus.title: Finding the nucleus
finding-the-nucleus.summary: Almost every alpha particle sails through gold foil. A very few bounce back — and that is enough to redraw the atom.

matter-waves.title: Matter waves
matter-waves.summary: Everything that moves has a wavelength. For an electron it is the size of an atom — and that changes everything.

the-halogens.title: The halogens
the-halogens.summary: Four elements one electron short of a full shell: the higher one always takes that electron from the lower.

the-noble-gases.title: The noble gases
the-noble-gases.summary: Full shells, no reactions — until 1962, when xenon was caught bonding to fluorine.

the-lanthanoid-contraction.title: The lanthanoid contraction
the-lanthanoid-contraction.summary: Fifteen elements, one more proton each time — and the ion gets smaller at every step.

the-actinoids.title: The actinoids
the-actinoids.summary: The same f-block pattern one row down — but radioactive, and with far more oxidation states.

overlapping-orbitals.title: Overlapping orbitals
overlapping-orbitals.summary: Two atoms come together until their orbitals overlap just enough — and how they overlap decides the kind of bond.

sigma-and-pi.title: Sigma and pi
sigma-and-pi.summary: One sigma bond between every pair of bonded atoms; a pi bond for each extra line in a double or triple bond.

closing-in.title: Closing in
closing-in.summary: A limit is where a function is heading as x closes in — whether or not it ever gets there.

breaks-and-holes.title: Breaks and holes
breaks-and-holes.summary: A graph you can draw without lifting the pen is continuous. There are three ways to have to lift it.

zooming-in.title: Zooming in
zooming-in.summary: Magnify a smooth curve enough and it becomes a straight line. A corner stays a corner for ever.

closing-the-gap.title: Closing the gap
closing-the-gap.summary: The slope between two points is an average. Slide one point into the other and it becomes the slope at a point.

the-slope-graph.title: The slope graph
the-slope-graph.summary: Measure the slope at every point and plot it: the result is a new function, the derivative.

bending-up-bending-down.title: Bending up, bending down
bending-up-bending-down.summary: The slope has a slope of its own. Its sign says which way the curve bends — and tells a hilltop from a valley.

the-growing-rectangle.title: The growing rectangle
the-growing-rectangle.summary: A product is an area. Nudge x and the area grows by two strips — and a corner that does not last.

links-in-a-chain.title: Links in a chain
links-in-a-chain.summary: A function of a function passes a small change along in two steps, stretching it each time. The stretches multiply.

round-the-circle.title: Round the circle
round-the-circle.summary: Some curves are not y = something. Their slopes can still be found — from the equation as it stands, or from a parameter.

the-best-box.title: The best box
the-best-box.summary: Cut a square from each corner of a sheet and fold up the sides. Too small a cut and the box is shallow; too big and it has no base.

rising-and-falling.title: Rising and falling
rising-and-falling.summary: The sign of the derivative is a map of the curve: where it climbs, where it drops, and where it turns.

tied-together.title: Tied together
tied-together.summary: Two quantities linked by an equation cannot change independently. Know how fast one is changing and you know the other.

sweeping-the-area.title: Sweeping the area
sweeping-the-area.summary: A line sweeps along a curve, collecting the area behind it. Plot that area as you go and a second curve appears — whose slope is the first.

undoing-the-slope.title: Undoing the slope
undoing-the-slope.summary: The area graph is a function whose slope is f — an antiderivative. Start collecting somewhere else and you get another one, the same shape moved up or down.

distance-from-speed.title: Distance from speed
distance-from-speed.summary: A car's velocity against time, in three straight pieces. The area collected under it is how far the car has gone; the slope of each piece is its acceleration.

molecules-in-a-box.title: Molecules in a box
molecules-in-a-box.summary: Pressure is molecules drumming on the walls; temperature is how hard they move.

how-fast-molecules-move.title: How fast molecules move
how-fast-molecules-move.summary: Faster than a bullet, at every speed at once — and barely getting anywhere.

heat-capacities-of-gases.title: Heat capacities of gases
heat-capacities-of-gases.summary: Count the ways a molecule can move and turn, and you can predict how much heat a gas soaks up.

slicing-it-thin.title: Slicing it thin
slicing-it-thin.summary: Cut the area under a curve into strips and add them up. The thinner the strips, the closer the total comes to the exact area — an accumulated total, like distance under a speed–time graph.

signed-area.title: Signed area
signed-area.summary: Below the axis a strip has negative height, so it counts negative. An integral can be zero while plenty is shaded.

between-the-curves.title: Between the curves
between-the-curves.summary: Stand each strip on the lower curve and stop it at the upper one. Its height is top minus bottom — and where the curves cross, top and bottom swap.

change-of-variable.title: Change of variable
change-of-variable.summary: Put u = g(x) and every strip moves to the u-axis: its width is multiplied by g′ and its height divided by g′. The area does not change, but the limits do.

two-areas-one-rectangle.title: Two areas, one rectangle
two-areas-one-rectangle.summary: Plot v against u. The area to the left of the curve and the area below it fill a rectangle — so ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du.

splitting-fractions.title: Splitting fractions
splitting-fractions.summary: One awkward fraction is two simple ones in disguise. Each simple one integrates to a logarithm, and their areas add.

first-law.title: Every joule accounted for
first-law.summary: Two bodies settle to one temperature, and a gas pushing a piston shares its heat between work and internal energy.

four-processes.title: Four ways to move a piston
four-processes.summary: Hold the temperature, the heat, the pressure or the volume fixed, and see which of Q, W and ΔU must vanish.

engines-and-fridges.title: Engines and fridges
engines-and-fridges.summary: Run a gas round a loop to turn heat into work, find the limit no engine can beat, then run it backwards to make cold.

charges-and-forces.title: Charges and forces
charges-and-forces.summary: Charge comes in whole electrons. Two charges push or pull as 1/r², and a third feels the vector sum of both.

fields-and-dipoles.title: Fields and dipoles
fields-and-dipoles.summary: The field is the force per coulomb. A +q and a −q side by side make a dipole, which a uniform field twists but does not move.

flux-and-gauss.title: Flux and Gauss's law
flux-and-gauss.summary: Count the field through a surface. Close the surface, and the count depends only on the charge inside.

follow-the-slopes.title: Follow the slopes
follow-the-slopes.summary: A differential equation tells you the slope at every point. Draw them all, and the solutions draw themselves. (Slope fields go beyond NCERT; they are the picture behind its methods.)

growth-and-cooling.title: Growth and cooling
growth-and-cooling.summary: When the rate of change is proportional to the amount, the answer is always an exponential: bacteria, radioactivity and a cup of tea.

solving-them.title: Solving them
solving-them.summary: Sort equations by order and degree, pick the method that fits, and finish a linear one with an integrating factor.

hills-of-potential.title: Hills of potential
hills-of-potential.summary: A charge raises a hill of potential around it. Walk a test charge over it: climbing costs work, walking round the hillside costs none.

storing-charge.title: Storing charge
storing-charge.summary: A conductor keeps the field out of its inside. Two conducting plates close together hold charge and energy — and a dielectric lets them hold more.

capacitors-together.title: Capacitors together
capacitors-together.summary: In series they share one charge; in parallel, one voltage. And when a charged capacitor meets an empty one, charge is kept but energy is not.

travelling-waves.title: Travelling waves
travelling-waves.summary: The wave runs along; the string only bobs up and down. What sets how fast it goes, and how long each wave is?

standing-waves.title: Standing waves
standing-waves.summary: Waves add where they meet. Trap a wave between two ends and only certain notes fit.

beats-and-doppler.title: Beats and Doppler
beats-and-doppler.summary: Two notes almost in tune throb. A passing siren drops in pitch. And every step back from a speaker takes some decibels off.

springs-and-pendulums.title: Springs and pendulums
springs-and-pendulums.summary: A block on a spring is the shadow of a point going round a circle. Find its phase, its period — and why a pendulum's bob does not matter.

energy-in-shm.title: Energy in SHM
energy-in-shm.summary: Kinetic and potential energy trade places twice a swing, and the total stays ½kA². Then join two springs and see how stiff the pair is.

damped-and-driven.title: Damped and driven
damped-and-driven.summary: Oil makes the swings die away; a well-timed push makes them grow. Find resonance — then twist a disc on a wire.

dipole-and-lines.title: The bar magnet
dipole-and-lines.summary: A short bar magnet is a magnetic dipole: its field falls as 1/r³, is twice as strong on its axis, and runs in closed loops.

the-earths-field.title: The Earth's field
the-earths-field.summary: The Earth's field points into the ground at the dip angle. Its horizontal part turns a compass; a dip circle shows the rest.

magnetic-matter.title: Magnetic matter
magnetic-matter.summary: Put a material in a field and it adds a little, takes a little, or adds a great deal — and iron remembers where it has been.

changing-flux.title: Changing flux
changing-flux.summary: Flux is field times the area it meets. Change it and the coil answers with an EMF — pushing back against the change.

rods-and-brakes.title: Rods and brakes
rods-and-brakes.summary: Move a conductor through a field and it becomes a cell — and the field drags on the current it makes.

coils-and-generators.title: Coils and generators
coils-and-generators.summary: A coil resists changes in its own current and stirs up EMFs in its neighbours. Spin one in a field and you have mains electricity.

drift-and-resistance.title: Drift and resistance
drift-and-resistance.summary: Electrons crawl through a wire at a millimetre a second. How long, thick, hot and what metal the wire is decides how hard they are to push.

cells-and-power.title: Cells and power
cells-and-power.summary: A real cell loses some of its EMF inside itself. Match the load to it for the most power, join cells to push harder, and watch a capacitor fill.

loops-and-bridges.title: Loops and bridges
loops-and-bridges.summary: Kirchhoff's two rules solve any circuit. A balanced bridge or potentiometer measures without a current — the galvanometer reads zero.

circling-charges.title: Charges that circle
circling-charges.summary: A magnetic field pushes a moving charge sideways, so it goes round — and every turn takes the same time, however fast it goes.

pushes-on-currents.title: Pushes on currents
pushes-on-currents.summary: A current is moving charge, so a field pushes on it too: on a wire, between two wires, and as a turning couple on a coil.

fields-of-currents.title: Fields from currents
fields-of-currents.summary: Every bit of current makes a field. Add them up — or use Ampère's law — for a wire, a loop, a solenoid and a toroid.

ac-phase-and-rms.title: Peaks, rms and phase
ac-phase-and-rms.summary: The mains turns like an arrow. In a coil the current trails the voltage by a quarter turn; in a capacitor it runs a quarter turn ahead.

ac-resonance-and-power.title: Resonance and power
ac-resonance-and-power.summary: Tune a circuit until its reactances cancel, find where the power goes, step voltages up and down, and let a capacitor and a coil pass energy back and forth.

em-waves-and-spectrum.title: Waves of E and B
em-waves-and-spectrum.summary: A changing electric field makes a magnetic one, and the two can travel on together at the speed of light — as radio, light or X-rays.

light-on-a-metal.title: Light on a metal
light-on-a-metal.summary: Shine light on a metal plate and electrons fly out — but only if the light's frequency is high enough, however bright it is.
light-on-a-metal.lab: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

stopping-the-electrons.title: Stopping the electrons
stopping-the-electrons.summary: Turn the collector negative until even the fastest electrons are turned back. That stopping potential measures K_max = hν − φ.
stopping-the-electrons.lab: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

photons-and-electron-waves.title: Photons and electron waves
photons-and-electron-waves.summary: Light comes in particles with energy hν and momentum h/λ — and electrons, fired at a crystal, diffract like waves.
photons-and-electron-waves.lab: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

tiny-and-dense.title: Tiny and dense
tiny-and-dense.summary: A nucleus is a few femtometres across, packed as densely as every other nucleus — and it weighs less than the pieces it is made of.

towards-iron.title: Towards iron
towards-iron.summary: Nucleons are held most tightly near iron. Split a heavy nucleus or join light ones, and the move towards iron sets energy free.

a-half-at-a-time.title: A half at a time
a-half-at-a-time.summary: No one can say when one atom will decay, but a crowd of them halves in a fixed time, again and again.

wavefronts-and-fringes.title: Wavefronts and fringes
wavefronts-and-fringes.summary: Watch wavelets bend a wavefront into glass, then send light through two slits and measure the fringes.

diffraction-and-resolution.title: Bright, dark and blurred
diffraction-and-resolution.summary: Read the brightness across the fringes, spread light through one slit, and find how close two stars can be.

polaroids-and-films.title: Polarised light and soap films
polaroids-and-films.summary: Turn one polaroid against another, polarise light by reflection, and find out why a soap film is coloured.

push-and-flow.title: Push and flow
push-and-flow.summary: A small push lifts a car, water races through a narrow pipe, and where it is fast its pressure is low.

thick-and-thin.title: Thick and thin
thick-and-thin.summary: Drag a plate over glycerine, drop a ball through it, and time its steady fall to measure how thick the liquid is.

drops-and-tubes.title: Drops and tubes
drops-and-tubes.summary: A liquid's surface pulls like a stretched skin: it squeezes drops and bubbles, and drags water up a narrow glass tube.

mirror-images.title: Images in mirrors
mirror-images.summary: Where a mirror puts the image, how big it is, and which way up — with every distance measured from the pole and given its sign.

lens-images.title: Lenses and power
lens-images.summary: Grind a lens to the focal length you need, find its images, and add a second lens to change its power.

trapped-light.title: Bend, trap and split
trapped-light.summary: Bend light into glass, trap it there beyond the critical angle, then send it through a prism and split it into colours.

looking-closer.title: Sky, eyes and telescopes
looking-closer.summary: Why the sky is blue and the sunset red, how spectacles fix an eye, and how two lenses make a microscope or a telescope.

building-units.title: Building units
building-units.summary: Seven base units make every other. Their powers — the dimensions — convert units, catch wrong formulas and even find new ones.

how-many-figures.title: How many figures?
how-many-figures.summary: An instrument's least count decides how many digits a reading can have — and every calculation can only keep as many as its weakest measurement.

errors-add-up.title: Errors add up
errors-add-up.summary: Every measurement carries an error, and every calculation inherits them — added for sums, added as percentages for products, and multiplied up by powers.

bands-and-holes.title: Bands and holes
bands-and-holes.summary: Why silicon is neither metal nor glass, how a few atoms of arsenic or boron change it, and what happens where p meets n.

one-way-street.title: A one-way street
one-way-street.summary: The diode lets current through one way only. Use it to turn AC into DC, then let a Zener hold the voltage steady.

light-and-logic.title: Light and logic
light-and-logic.summary: Junctions that make light and junctions that use it — then the transistor, and the gates it builds.

stretch-and-scale.title: Stretch and scale
stretch-and-scale.summary: Read one hotness on three scales, then watch rails stretch, strips curl and water break the rules.

down-the-rod.title: Down the rod
down-the-rod.summary: Push heat along a lagged rod, then through two slabs in a row, and find the temperature where they meet.

glow-and-cool.title: Glow and cool
glow-and-cool.summary: Breezes that turn round at night, bodies that glow red then white, and a cup of tea cooling on the table.

pulled-by-a-string.title: Pulled by a string
pulled-by-a-string.summary: Two blocks, one string: write F = ma for each, and let the string tie the answers together.

lifts-and-moving-frames.title: Lifts and moving frames
lifts-and-moving-frames.summary: A scale in a lift, a bob in a car: what you feel depends on how your frame accelerates.

round-the-bend.title: Round the bend
round-the-bend.summary: Something must pull a car into its curve: friction, a tilted road, or both. And a swinging bob does the same with its string.

up-and-down.title: Up and down
up-and-down.summary: A ball thrown straight up slows, stops and falls back — and its acceleration never changes once.

along-the-road.title: Along the road
along-the-road.summary: How one car moves as seen from another, and how fast a cart goes when its acceleration will not keep still.

rivers-and-rain.title: Rivers and rain
rivers-and-rain.summary: A boat is carried by the water it moves through; rain falls differently on someone who is walking.

circles-and-slopes.title: Circles and slopes
circles-and-slopes.summary: Going round at a steady speed is still accelerating; and up a hillside, 45° is no longer the best throw.

curved-mirrors.title: Concave and convex mirrors
curved-mirrors.summary: Move an object towards a curved mirror and watch the image move, grow, shrink and flip — then find where torches, shaving mirrors and rear-view mirrors use each kind.

seeing-clearly.title: Seeing clearly
seeing-clearly.summary: The parts of the eye, why some eyes cannot see far or near, and the power of the spectacle lens that fixes each.

rainbow-and-sky.title: Rainbows and the blue sky
rainbow-and-sky.summary: A prism splits white light into seven colours, raindrops make a rainbow, and air turns the sky blue and the rising sun red.

squeeze-and-shear.title: Squeeze and shear
squeeze-and-shear.summary: Press a cube equally on every face and it shrinks; push its top sideways and it leans. Each has its own modulus.

thinner-as-it-stretches.title: Thinner as it stretches
thinner-as-it-stretches.summary: Pull a wire and it gets longer — and a little thinner. The ratio of the two strains belongs to the material.

how-g-changes.title: How g changes
how-g-changes.summary: Climb above the Earth, dig down into it, walk to the pole: g is 9.8 m/s² only where you started.

falling-together.title: Falling together
falling-together.summary: Gravity as force per kilogram, the point where the Earth and the Moon pull equally, and why an astronaut 400 km up floats.

the-cost-of-climbing.title: The cost of climbing
the-cost-of-climbing.summary: A satellite's kinetic, potential and total energy, how tightly it is bound, and what it costs to move it higher.

shifting-the-axis.title: Shifting the axis
shifting-the-axis.summary: Move the axis away from the centre and the body gets harder to turn — by exactly Md². And for a flat body, two axes in its plane add up to the third.

the-rolling-race.title: The rolling race
the-rolling-race.summary: A rolling wheel is moving and turning at once, and its bottom point stands still. Let four shapes go down one slope and the one with its mass nearest the middle wins.

balancing-act.title: Balancing act
balancing-act.summary: A body at rest needs no net force and no net torque. Balance a see-saw, spot a couple, and find what keeps a ladder from sliding.

balance-and-break-up.title: Balance and break-up
balance-and-break-up.summary: Find the point a rod of masses balances on, then burst a shell in mid-air and watch its centre of mass carry on regardless.
balance-and-break-up.lab: Centre of Mass, Collisions and Energy

glancing-blows-and-rockets.title: Glancing blows and rockets
glancing-blows-and-rockets.summary: Momentum is a vector: it is kept along x and along y when pucks glance off each other — and a rocket gains it by throwing mass away.
glancing-blows-and-rockets.lab: Centre of Mass, Collisions and Energy

the-area-and-the-rate.title: The area and the rate
the-area-and-the-rate.summary: When a force changes as it moves, its work is the area under its graph. How fast that work is done is the power.
the-area-and-the-rate.lab: Centre of Mass, Collisions and Energy

loops-and-hollows.title: Loops and hollows
loops-and-hollows.summary: Whirl a ball in a vertical circle fast enough that the string never goes slack, then read a ball's whole motion off its potential-energy curve.
loops-and-hollows.lab: Centre of Mass, Collisions and Energy

push-and-rub.title: Pushes, pulls and rubs
push-and-rub.summary: Push a box with a friend. Forces add, take away, or balance, and friction always pushes back.

sharp-and-wide.title: Sharp points, wide straps
sharp-and-wide.summary: The same push on a smaller area makes a bigger pressure. Pressure = force ÷ area.

the-pull-of-gravity.title: The pull of gravity
the-pull-of-gravity.summary: Every mass pulls on every other. The Earth's pull makes things fall, and gives them weight.

spans-and-scales.title: Spans and scales
spans-and-scales.summary: Measure a desk with your hand. Then let the teacher try — and see why we need a standard unit.

reading-a-ruler.title: Reading a ruler
reading-a-ruler.summary: Start at any mark, look straight down, and measure a curved line with a thread.

swings-and-spins.title: Swings and spins
swings-and-spins.summary: Straight, round, to and fro or spinning — then time a pendulum and make it tick once a second.

adding-in-pairs.title: Adding in pairs
adding-in-pairs.summary: A staircase that climbs by the same step each time. Turn a copy upside down on top of it and the sum falls out.

halves-for-ever.title: Halves for ever
halves-for-ever.summary: Multiply by the same ratio each time. Some sums run away; others close in on a number they never quite reach.

means-and-blocks.title: Means and blocks
means-and-blocks.summary: The geometric mean stands inside a semicircle whose radius is the average. Then stack blocks to add squares and cubes.

the-argand-plane.title: The Argand plane
the-argand-plane.summary: a + ib is a point: so far along, so far up. That gives every complex number a length and a direction.

turn-and-stretch.title: Turn and stretch
turn-and-stretch.summary: Multiplying complex numbers multiplies their lengths and adds their angles — so some multiplications are pure turns.

the-discriminant.title: The discriminant
the-discriminant.summary: b² − 4ac says whether a parabola cuts the x-axis, touches it, or misses it — and when it misses, the roots are a complex pair.

where-the-roots-lie.title: Where the roots lie
where-the-roots-lie.summary: Without solving: the sign of a·f(k), the discriminant and the vertex say which side of k the roots are on.

multiply-the-choices.title: Multiply the choices
multiply-the-choices.summary: One choice after another multiplies. Fill slots from a set of letters and the count is a product you never have to list.

choose-a-team.title: Choose a team
choose-a-team.summary: A team does not care about order, so every team is counted r! times among the arrangements. Then share out sweets that cannot be told apart.

seats-and-necklaces.title: Seats and necklaces
seats-and-necklaces.summary: Glue two friends together, keep two rivals apart, turn the table, flip the necklace, and swap letters that look the same.

pascals-triangle.title: Pascal's triangle
pascals-triangle.summary: Each number is the sum of the two above it, and row n holds the coefficients of (a + b)ⁿ. Then pick any term out of an expansion without writing the rest.

two-dice.title: Two dice
two-dice.summary: Throw two dice and there are 36 equally likely outcomes. Count the ones you want and you have the probability.

given-that.title: Given that
given-that.summary: Once you know something has happened, the outcomes that did not fit are gone. Probability is counted again in what is left.

testing-positive.title: Testing positive
testing-positive.summary: A test that catches 90% of the ill, with only 5% false alarms. You test positive. How worried should you be?

counting-successes.title: Counting successes
counting-successes.summary: A number decided by chance has a probability for each value. Draw them as bars, find the balance point, and toss coins until the bars appear.

feel-it-read-it.title: Feel it, read it
feel-it-read-it.summary: Why your hands can disagree about the same water, and how to read a thermometer instead.

heat-on-the-move.title: Heat on the move
heat-on-the-move.summary: Pins dropping off a rod, a purple streak in a beaker, and two cans in the sun: three ways heat travels.

breeze-by-the-sea.title: Breeze by the sea
breeze-by-the-sea.summary: Land heats up and cools down faster than water, so the seaside breeze turns round between day and night.

heat-and-fuses.title: Hot wires and fuses
heat-and-fuses.summary: A current heats a wire: H = I²Rt. A fuse uses that heat to keep a house safe.

magnets-from-current.title: Magnets from a current
magnets-from-current.summary: A coil round a nail becomes a magnet. Field lines circle a wire and run through a solenoid like a bar magnet.

motors-and-generators.title: Motors and generators
motors-and-generators.summary: A current in a magnetic field is pushed: that turns a motor. A magnet moving in a coil makes a current: that is a generator.

points-in-space.title: Points in space
points-in-space.summary: Every point has a position vector from the origin. Mix two of them and you land between the points; divide by the length and you get a direction.

shadows-and-areas.title: Shadows and areas
shadows-and-areas.summary: Two ways to multiply arrows. The dot product gives a number — how much one points along the other. The cross product gives a new arrow, standing up from the parallelogram they make.

boxes-and-planes.title: Boxes and planes
boxes-and-planes.summary: Three vectors make a box, and its volume is one number: [a b c]. A normal vector and one number make a plane — and tell you how far any point is from it.

lines-that-miss.title: Lines that miss
lines-that-miss.summary: In a plane, two lines that are not parallel must cross. In space they can pass each other by — and there is exactly one shortest way across the gap.

middle-of-the-marks.title: The middle of the marks
middle-of-the-marks.summary: Three ways to say where the middle of a class's marks is — and the one a single far-out mark can drag about.

how-spread-out.title: How spread out?
how-spread-out.summary: Two classes can share a mean and still be nothing alike. Measure how far the marks stray from the middle — then stretch and slide them.

grouped-into-classes.title: Grouped into classes
grouped-into-classes.summary: Thirty or fifty values are too many to list. Count them into classes, draw the bars, and find the middle and the spread from the table alone.

where-i-and-j-land.title: Where î and ĵ land
where-i-and-j-land.summary: A 2 × 2 matrix moves the whole plane. Its two columns say where î and ĵ go — and everything else follows.

the-area-scale.title: The area scale
the-area-scale.summary: ad − bc is how many times bigger every area gets — negative if the picture flips, zero if it is squashed flat.

undoing-a-matrix.title: Undoing a matrix
undoing-a-matrix.summary: A⁻¹ = adj A / |A| puts the plane back — unless |A| = 0. And the transpose sorts matrices into symmetric, skew-symmetric and orthogonal.

two-lines-one-point.title: Two lines, one point
two-lines-one-point.summary: Two equations are two lines and AX = B. If |A| ≠ 0 they cross at one point; if |A| = 0 they are parallel or the same line.

sines-and-cosines.title: Sines and cosines
sines-and-cosines.summary: Two sides and the angle between them fix a triangle. The cosine rule finds the third side; the sine rule finds the angles.

out-of-reach.title: Out of reach
out-of-reach.summary: Nobody climbs a tower to measure it. An angle and a distance on the ground are enough.

centres-of-a-triangle.title: Centres of a triangle
centres-of-a-triangle.summary: A circle through the corners, a circle inside touching the sides, and a line that three centres always share.

push-and-lift.title: Push and lift
push-and-lift.summary: A force does work only when something moves. Work = force × distance, measured in joules.

watts-and-units.title: Watts and units
watts-and-units.summary: Power is how fast work is done. The electricity bill counts energy in kilowatt hours.

adding-angles.title: Adding angles
adding-angles.summary: Turn by A, then by B. Where you land is A + B — and its coordinates are built from the sines and cosines of A and B.

every-solution.title: Every solution
every-solution.summary: A line y = k cuts a sine wave again and again. One formula with a whole number n finds every crossing.

running-backwards.title: Running backwards
running-backwards.summary: Many angles share a sine, so sin⁻¹ has to choose one. It always chooses from the same half-wave: the principal value.

small-angles.title: Small angles
small-angles.summary: For a small angle in radians, sin θ and tan θ are almost θ itself, and cos θ is almost 1 − θ²/2. Physics uses this all the time — but how small is small?

slicing-the-cone.title: Slicing the cone
slicing-the-cone.summary: Cut a double cone with a plane and four curves come out. One number, the eccentricity, tells them apart.

pins-and-string.title: Two pins and a string
pins-and-string.summary: Loop a string round two pins and pull it tight: the pencil draws an ellipse. Keep a difference fixed instead, and you get a hyperbola.

touching-the-curve.title: Touching the curve
touching-the-curve.summary: Each conic has a one-line formula for its tangent. The tangent also explains why a dish aerial works.

forms-of-a-line.title: The forms of a line
forms-of-a-line.summary: Two points fix a line. Its slope, its intercepts and its distance from the origin are all in its equation, whichever form you write it in.

lines-at-an-angle.title: Lines at an angle
lines-at-an-angle.summary: Two lines cross at an angle you can work out from their slopes alone; a point sits a distance from a line you can work out from its equation.

line-meets-circle.title: Where a line meets a circle
line-meets-circle.summary: A circle is every point one radius from a centre. Whether a line cuts it, touches it or misses it comes down to one distance.

tangents-and-radical-axis.title: Tangents and the radical axis
tangents-and-radical-axis.summary: A tangent meets the radius at right angles. From that one fact come the tangent's equation, its length from a point, and the line where two circles' tangents are equal.

wheels-and-tins.title: Wheels and tins
wheels-and-tins.summary: Roll a wheel once and it lays its rim along the ground. Peel the label off a tin and it is a rectangle.

area-of-a-circle.title: Area of a circle
area-of-a-circle.summary: Cut a circle into thin slices and lay them point up, point down: they make a rectangle πr long and r tall.

cones-and-spheres.title: Cones and spheres
cones-and-spheres.summary: Three cones of water fill a cylinder. Balls, bowls, capsules and ice-cream cones are built from the same few shapes.

same-shape-new-size.title: Same shape, new size
same-shape-new-size.summary: A photo enlarged, a map shrunk, a tower and its shadow: the same shape at a different size. Equal angles, sides in the same ratio.

hops-below-zero.title: Hops below zero
hops-below-zero.summary: A frog hops along the number line, right past zero and out the other side. Add, subtract, and read a cold night's temperature.

turning-round-twice.title: Turning round twice
turning-round-twice.summary: Multiplying is hopping from 0 again and again. A minus sign turns the frog round — so what do two minus signs do?

between-any-two.title: Between any two
between-any-two.summary: Fractions can be negative too. Place them, put them in order, and zoom into the gap between two of them — it never runs out.

share-it-fairly.title: Share it fairly
share-it-fairly.summary: Share sweets in a ratio, spot ratios that are secretly the same, and scale a recipe up with the unitary method.

out-of-a-hundred.title: Out of a hundred
out-of-a-hundred.summary: Per cent means out of 100. Use it for a sale, a shopkeeper's profit, and money that grows in a bank.

powers-big-and-small.title: Powers, big and small
powers-big-and-small.summary: Multiply 2 by itself, learn the laws of powers, write the Sun's distance in standard form, and find square roots.

sets-and-relations.title: Sets and relations
sets-and-relations.summary: Overlap two sets and count what they hold between them, then test a relation for the three properties that make it an equivalence.

arrows-and-graphs.title: Arrows and graphs
arrows-and-graphs.summary: A function sends every element of its domain to exactly one image. Draw it as arrows and as a graph, and see when no two inputs share an output.

chains-and-inverses.title: Chains and inverses
chains-and-inverses.summary: Feed one function's output into another, and find out which functions can be run backwards.

measuring-turns.title: Measuring turns
measuring-turns.summary: An angle is an amount of turn. Measure it, name it, and find its partners on a straight line.

parallel-lines-and-triangles.title: Parallel lines and triangles
parallel-lines-and-triangles.summary: Tilt a line until it is parallel, then find out why every triangle's angles make a straight line.

congruence-and-parallelograms.title: Same shape, same size
congruence-and-parallelograms.summary: Which parts fix a triangle, and what makes a parallelogram special.

angles-in-a-circle.title: Angles in a circle
angles-in-a-circle.summary: A chord looks the same from everywhere on one arc — and twice as big from the centre.

tally-marks-and-bars.title: Tally marks and bar graphs
tally-marks-and-bars.summary: Count a class's answers in fives, then draw them as pictures and bars.

how-likely-is-it.title: How likely is it?
how-likely-is-it.summary: From impossible to certain. Then toss a coin a thousand times and watch chance settle down.

favourable-over-possible.title: Favourable over possible
favourable-over-possible.summary: No tossing needed: count the outcomes. A bag of balls, a deck of 52 cards and a die.

sort-and-dissolve.title: Sort it, dissolve it
sort-and-dissolve.summary: Shiny or dull, see-through or not, floats or sinks — then stir salt into water until no more will go.

separate-and-protect.title: Pull it apart, keep it bright
separate-and-protect.summary: Pick the right way to pull each mixture apart — then find out what a nail needs to rust.

particles-on-the-move.title: Particles on the move
particles-on-the-move.summary: Everything is made of tiny moving particles. Heat them and they speed up — and the fastest escape as vapour, cooling what is left.

primes-and-roots.title: Primes and roots
primes-and-roots.summary: Break numbers down to their primes, find HCF and LCM, and put √2, √3 and √5 on the number line.

growing-patterns.title: Growing patterns
growing-patterns.summary: Count matchsticks and dots, find the rule for any term, and add expressions with tiles that only join their own kind.

parabolas-and-progressions.title: Parabolas and progressions
parabolas-and-progressions.summary: See where a quadratic's graph meets the x-axis, then build an AP and add it up the quick way.

metal-or-non-metal.title: Metal or non-metal?
metal-or-non-metal.summary: Shiny, bendy and ringing — or dull and brittle. Sort the elements, meet the rule-breakers, and watch metals corrode.

which-metal-wins.title: Which metal wins?
which-metal-wins.summary: Drop a metal into another metal's solution: the more reactive one pushes the other out. Then see what is oxidised and what is reduced.

fizz-ph-and-salts.title: Fizz, pH and salts
fizz-ph-and-salts.summary: Acids fizz with metals and carbonates — test the gas. Then read the pH scale, and meet the salts in your kitchen.

atoms-to-formulae.title: Atoms to formulae
atoms-to-formulae.summary: Atoms join into molecules, ions join into compounds — and a formula says exactly how many of each.
atoms-to-formulae.lab: Atoms, Molecules and the Periodic Table

counting-in-moles.title: Counting in moles
counting-in-moles.summary: Atoms are far too small to count one by one, so chemists count them by weighing — a mole at a time.
counting-in-moles.lab: Atoms, Molecules and the Periodic Table

ordering-the-elements.title: Ordering the elements
ordering-the-elements.summary: Three chemists, three tries at putting the elements in order — and the patterns the final table shows.
